//: Advisories accepted after analysis. scripts/audit-gate.mjs fails on anything not listed here, AND fails when a listed advisory no longer appears — so an entry cannot outlive its reason. Never add an entry to silence something reachable; fix that at the root.

accepted.reason: Not reachable here. The only path is prisma -> @prisma/config -> deepmerge-ts, and @prisma/config calls deepmerge in exactly one place: loadConfigTsOrJs(), which merges prisma.config.ts layers through c12. This repo has no prisma.config.* file, and that input is a developer's own config rather than anything a request can influence. CVE-2026-40345 is a stack-exhaustion DoS whose CVSS 8.2 assumes an application feeding attacker-controlled JSON to deepmerge's public API; an attacker able to edit the Prisma config already has code execution.
accepted.whyNotFixed: No release on the Prisma 6 line has the fix: 6.19.3, the last 6.x, pins "deepmerge-ts": "7.1.5" exactly, with no range. As of 2026-11-27 the only stable release with the fix is Prisma 7.10.1 (@prisma/config 7.10.1 pins deepmerge-ts 8.0.2); every earlier 7.x still pins 7.1.5. Moving to it is a major upgrade (Prisma 6 to 7) with breaking changes, its own project rather than a dependency bump, and it would not clear the gate on its own: @prisma/config 7.10.1 also pins effect 3.20.0, which GHSA-7589-6fvf-x4pw (accepted below) still covers. `npm audit fix --force` proposes prisma 6.12.0, a major downgrade. An npm override would force past an exact pin across a major boundary, which this project does not do.
accepted.tracking: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx and https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues/30052 (the earlier fix PR, https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/30054, was closed without merging; the fix reached Prisma 7.10.1 another way). Delete this entry when the project upgrades to Prisma 7.10.1 or later, or when a Prisma 6 release moves to deepmerge-ts 8; the gate fails when the advisory stops appearing, which is the reminder.

accepted.reason: Not reachable here. The only path is prisma -> @prisma/config -> effect (npm ls effect), and no file in src, scripts or tests imports effect. The flaw (CVE-2026-121707) is a ReDoS in the regex that Schema.TemplateLiteral compiles; @prisma/config never uses Schema.TemplateLiteral (its dist/index.js uses only Struct, String, optional, Literal, Union and similar schemas). @prisma/config validates a prisma.config.* file, this repo has none, and it runs only inside the Prisma CLI (generate, migrate) on a developer machine or in CI. The @prisma/client runtime does not import effect; @prisma/config appears in it only as text in bundled package metadata. No request input ever reaches it.
accepted.whyNotFixed: The fix is effect 3.22.1, but no stable Prisma release accepts it. @prisma/config pins "effect" exactly, with no range: 6.19.3 (installed, the latest 6.x) pins 3.21.0 and 7.10.1 pins 3.20.0. Prisma 8 drops effect, but on 2026-11-27 it exists only as release candidates (8.0.0-rc.36), and it is a major upgrade. An npm override would force past an exact pin, which this project does not do.
accepted.tracking: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7589-6fvf-x4pw . When a stable Prisma release depends on effect 3.22.1 or later (or on no effect at all, as Prisma 8 does), upgrade prisma and @prisma/client and delete this entry; the gate fails when the advisory stops appearing, which is the reminder.
